To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thymuses of hibernating ground squirrels can be used to decelerate the age-related involution of the rat thymus.
thymic transplantation in aging rats restores the thymus to its youthful state, and that thymus tissue of the hibernating ground squirrels is more effective in this respect than that of the rats.
thymus transplantation from hibernating ground squirrels to rats with an age-related involution of the gland results in the restoration of the thymic structure and function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the hibernating thymus in age-related involution of the rat thymus.
studying the role of thymic factors in the regulation of immune processes and adaptation in ground squirrels.
